transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: Let me compare per-service span behavior between the normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2) p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT 'normal' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2) p95_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=400 OR attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend','geo','rate','profile','reservation') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'abnormal', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,2), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=400 OR attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend','geo','rate','profile','reservation') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,4,1,3

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT 'N' p, time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod FROM normal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT 'A', time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT 'N', time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM normal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT 'A', time, metric, value, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_metrics_sum) SELECT service_name, metric, p, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT pod) pods, round(avg(value),3) avg_v, round(max(value),3) max_v FROM a WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','geo','frontend','memcached-rate-1','mongodb-rate') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts','container.cpu.time','k8s.pod.network.errors','container.memory.usage','k8s.pod.cpu.time','container.cpu.utilization') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: Rate and search show no resource saturation or restarts. Next I'll pair each search client span with its rate server span to see where the extra time sits.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, c.service_name, c.span_name, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) client_ms, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,1) server_ms, round(avg(c.duration-s.duration)/1e6,1) gap_ms, round(quantile_cont(c.duration-s.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) gap_p50 FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', c.service_name, c.span_name, c.attr_k8s_pod_name, s.attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1), round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,1), round(avg(c.duration-s.duration)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(c.duration-s.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: The logs show no error templates, and the only changed connection is search→rate. I have enough to write up the answer.

input.reflection: Findings: only the frontend /hotels path (search.Search/Nearby) degraded: frontend server ~1.8s vs 7ms normal. Search server 1.8s; search->rate GetRates client 1.78s but rate server span 0.4ms, so ~1.7s gap is in flight between search and rate. Search->geo calls normal (0.4ms), so it's connection-specific. No restarts, no uptime reset, no CPU/memory saturation on search or rate, no error status codes, no log errors. No hubble metrics exist. Gap is in-flight time with peer answering quickly, matching network_delay (on the search-rate connection). Propagation: rate -> search -> frontend. Name search as the faulty end of the connection with network_delay (other end rate).
